When the annealing temperature is below 700 ℃, the recrystallized grains are too small to form a soft domain that contributes to a heterogeneous microstructure. Con - versely, when the annealing temperature exceeds 700 ℃, the growth of recrystallized grains, twin boundary fraction, and twin boundary density becomes too rapid to maintain the hard domain.
